title: Refined K-Type Occurrence Proposition
body_html:
Refined K-Type Occurrence Proposition

If a covering datum \(\widetilde D\) for \(G\) has nonzero occurrence in the oscillator representation for \(V'\), then there exist a \(K\)-type datum \(\Sigma\) equivalent to \(\widetilde D\) and a target \(K\)-type datum \(\Sigma'\) such that \(\Sigma'\) is a theta lift of \(\Sigma\), and the corresponding \(K\times K'\)-type occurs in the generalized lattice model.
proof_html: The proof is by induction on the number of positive-depth blocks. The occurrence vector choice supercuspidal_theta.occurrence_vector_choice uses the building-indexed sum formula to choose \(x''\) and a vector \(w\) whose moment map matches the top-depth part of the source datum. Kim-Murnaghan conjugacy moves this moment value into block-diagonal form. The target top-block nondegenerate splitting supercuspidal_theta.target_top_block_nondegenerate_splitting and target lattice block splitting supercuspidal_theta.target_lattice_block_splitting split the target space and lattice function into top and lower blocks. The converse off-diagonal oscillator factorization supercuspidal_theta.converse_off_diagonal_oscillator_factorization factors the residual oscillator action so the lower block occurrence can be isolated. The top block is adjusted by positive-depth moment-map surjectivity supercuspidal_theta.positive_depth_moment_map_surjectivity to satisfy \(M({}^bw)={}^b\Gamma\), while the lower block is handled by induction. Combining the two blocks gives the required lifted datum.
